blocks.html: Ulpian in a certain place, speaking of a legacy made by a testator on condition that the legatee should swear, says that such a condition must be rejected, and that the legatee may boldly demand the legacy without taking the oath with which the testator charged him: so that, says he, he may neither lose the legacy by being unwilling to swear, nor win it by perjuring himself. For there are some, says the Jurisconsult, too ready to swear, in contempt of religion; others fearful of the divine power even to superstition, so that even of things which they know and are well assured of, they nevertheless would not, nor would dare to, swear a2.

notes.citation: Digest 28.7 (De condicionibus institutionum), l. Quae sub condicione (D. 28.7.8 pr.–§ 1, Ulpian)
notes.original: l. quæ ſub conditione. D de cond. inſt
notes.gloss: Quae sub condicione iurisiurandi relinquuntur, a praetore reprobantur: dispositions left under condition of an oath are disallowed by the praetor, who provides that the beneficiary shall neither lose the inheritance or legacy by omitting the condition nor be compelled to swear shamefully; for some are too ready to swear in contempt of religion, others too timid through fear of the godhead, even to superstition — Coras's whole annotation is a paraphrase of this law.
